title: The Made Object
text:
Postmodern fiction frequently rejects the notion of a single, authoritative meaning. Instead, writers invite readers to assemble the text themselves, often through fragmented chapters, shifting narrators, and deliberate contradictions. Such experiments can be disorienting, yet many critics argue that this disorientation is the point. The reader becomes an active participant rather than a passive observer.

Experimental novelists also draw attention to the act of writing itself. A narrator may admit that he is inventing characters, or a footnote may interrupt the story to comment on its own construction. By exposing these mechanisms, the author reminds readers that every story is a made object. Consequently, the boundary between fiction and criticism grows increasingly blurred.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do postmodern writers often reject?
options: The idea that readers are passive

questions.text: What can a footnote do, according to the second paragraph?
options: It introduces new characters into the plot
It interrupts the story to comment on its construction
It replaces the narrator with the author

questions.text: What do many critics believe about the disorientation caused by postmodern experiments?
options: It is an intended part of the works' purpose
It shows that the author has failed
It makes the books unsuitable for adults
It is caused by poor editing

questions.text: What is the most likely effect of exposing the mechanisms of storytelling on the reader?
options: The reader becomes more aware of the text as a constructed object
The reader stops questioning the story
The reader feels certain about the truth of the events
The reader loses interest in the genre

paragraph_translations: La ficción posmoderna con frecuencia rechaza la idea de un significado único e incuestionable. En cambio, los escritores invitan al lector a armar el texto por sí mismo, a menudo mediante capítulos fragmentados, narradores cambiantes y contradicciones deliberadas. Tales experimentos pueden resultar desorientadores, pero muchos críticos sostienen que esa desorientación es precisamente el objetivo. El lector se convierte en un participante activo y no en un observador pasivo.

Los novelistas experimentales también llaman la atención sobre el acto mismo de escribir. Un narrador puede admitir que está inventando personajes, o una nota al pie puede interrumpir la historia para comentar su propia construcción. Al exponer estos mecanismos, el autor recuerda a los lectores que toda historia es un objeto construido. En consecuencia, la frontera entre la ficción y la crítica se vuelve cada vez más difusa.
